paper_metadata.title: Longitudinal Changes in Diffusion Tensor Imaging Following Mild Traumatic Brain Injury and Correlation With Outcome

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population, recruitment source (ED), and explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria based on WHO standards. The use of a matched control group and consecutive enrollment helps limit selection bias.

items.evidence_snippet: We have conducted the "reliable change indices" analysis for all of NPTs in the present study. This method provides an estimate of the probability that a given difference score would not be obtained by chance
items.reasoning: The use of Reliable Change Indices (RCI) specifically addresses the reliability of the outcome measurements over time.

items.evidence_snippet: Statistical analysis was performed using the "randomize" command in FSL. The number of permutations was set to 10,000, and correction for multiple comparisons was achieved using threshold-free cluster enhancement (TFCE) with a family-wise error (FWE) rate of P < 0.05.
items.reasoning: The imaging and clinical statistical strategies are described in detail.

items.evidence_snippet: We mainly focused on the main time effect of the structural integrity of white matter (WM) fibers and its relationship with the initial neuropsychological measures.
items.reasoning: The model focuses on the hypothesized longitudinal changes and their correlation with clinical outcomes.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Longitudinal analysis, via repeated-measures ANOVA, was conducted to examine changes in both neuropsychological assessments and imaging FA metric as a function of recovery.
items.reasoning: Repeated-measures ANOVA is the standard approach for this 3-timepoint longitudinal design.

items.label: Reporting of results

items.evidence_snippet: The FA value of these three tracts presented no significant associations with the DSC at any specific time points (all for P > 0.2).
